But poor railway facilities, limited train tickets and a shortage of visitor services remain major obstacles to turning that potential into a thriving tourism destination. Situated about 165 kilometers from Bojnurd, the capital of North Khorasan province in northeastern Iran, Jajarm offers opportunities to experience rural life and a slower pace of travel without the costs often associated with more developed tourist centers. One of the area's distinctive landmarks is Jajarm railway station, a historical building that has served as the province's only active passenger rail connection to Iran's national railway network. The station, whose origins date to 1930 according to its glazed brick tiles, was inscribed on Iran's national industrial heritage list in 2019. Built during the early Pahlavi period, the approximately 33-by-15.9-meter structure features a stone facade and turquoise tilework. It once formed part of a larger railway workers' complex, of which only the station's administrative building and a water reservoir remain. full_text: Still haven't filed your taxes? Here's what you need to know So far this tax season, the IRS has received more than 90 million income tax returns for 2022. So far this tax season, the IRS has received more than 100 million income tax returns for 2022. That means tens of millions of households have yet to file their returns. If yours is among them, here are some last-minute tax-filing tips to keep in mind as the Tuesday, April 18 deadline approaches. Not everyone has to file on April 18:If you live in a federally declared disaster area, have a business there — or have relevant tax documents stored by businesses in that area — it’s likely the IRS has already extended the filing and payment deadlines for you.Hereis where you can find the specific extension dates for each disaster area. Thanks to many rounds of extreme weather in recent months, for instance, tax filers in most of California — which accounts for 10% to 15% of all federal filers — have already been granted an extension until Oct. 16 to file and to pay, according to an IRS spokesperson.
